_provenance.notes: Wild Alaska salmon quality is graded by flesh color (via the SalmoFan colorimetric scale), oil content, size, and freshness. Sockeye roe (ikura) is also graded by maturity stage and color. These grades directly determine ex-vessel price premiums. Copper River Chinook commands the highest premium due to highest oil content (omega-3 rich) and deep red color. Hatchery-origin chum salmon caught near saltwater entry points have higher oil content than those caught further upstream.

flesh_color_grading.description: SalmoFan colorimetric scale used by Alaska salmon industry to grade flesh color
flesh_color_grading.scale: 1-34 (SalmoFan Linear by DSM/Hoffman-LaRoche). Higher = deeper red. Wild sockeye typically 25-34.

Sockeye_Bristol_Bay.notes: Deepest red. Highest astaxanthin. Most valuable color.

Chinook_Copper_River.notes: Varies — can be white/red. Red Copper River Chinook commands $2-3/lb premium over white.

Chinook_White_Flesh.notes: Approx 15-25% of Chinook have white/cream flesh (inherited trait, not hatchery). Lower value — $1-2/lb less than red flesh.

Pink_Salmon.notes: Lighter pink. Lower fat. Primarily canned market.

Chum_Salmon_ocean.notes: Ocean-caught chum much higher quality than river-caught.

Chum_Salmon_river.notes: River-caught chum (keta) severely degraded color — primarily dog food/low-grade markets.

omega3_fat_content_by_species.description: Omega-3 fatty acid content (EPA + DHA combined) per 100g cooked serving — marketing and nutritional data
omega3_fat_content_by_species.source: USDA National Nutrient Database + published analyses

species.notes: Highest omega-3 of any wild salmon. Copper River Chinook averages 2.4g — the highest of any commercially caught fish.
Consistent and high. ASMI markets as premium omega-3 source.
Higher omega-3 but from feed — not from wild marine diet. Different fatty acid profile.
Lowest wild Alaska salmon omega-3 but still significant.
Lower fat white fish — valuable for other nutrients.
Low fat — the 'lean protein' selling point. 3B lbs/year global catch.

roe_grading.description: Alaska salmon roe (ikura) grading system — used by Japanese buyers and ASMI
roe_grading.notes: Roe quality is critical — a 10-25% price differential between grades A, B, and C. Grade depends on maturity stage (1-5), egg integrity, color, and oil content.

Grade_A.description: Stage 2-3 maturity. Firm, intact eggs. Bright orange-red. Maximum oil content. Japanese market premium.

Grade_B.description: Stage 3-4 maturity. Slightly softer eggs. Good color. Standard export quality.

Grade_C.description: Stage 4-5 maturity. Soft eggs. Lighter color. Domestic market or lower-value export.
